Hi Keith,
  what about using a subset:

library(ggplot2)
library(plyr)

dat <- data.frame(a = 1:50, b = rnorm(50))

ggplot(dat, aes(a, b)) + geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(subset = .(b > 0 ), color = "green")

# for help on the plyr function used by subset
.?


-Allan
R 2.15.1; plyr_1.7.1     ggplot2_0.9.1  reshape2_1.2.1


On Tuesday, 10 July 2012 16:19:29 UTC-4, keith p. kolley wrote:
is there a way to not plot smoothed data that is less than zero without changing the default maximum on the y axis?

my dataset is very noisy so i'm running it through a geom_smoother(method="loess"). the problem is that the difference between maximum y limit  from (geom_smoother)  and the maximum y limit from (geom_points) can be quite drastic and points below 0 do not make physical sense. i'm trying to limit the smoothed data, or at least the drawing of the smoothed data, to points > 0. is there a way to do something like coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,'auto')) or coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,max(geom_smoother$y))).  i'm thinking that my only option is to smooth the data myself, ifelse(y<0,0,y), and then call geom_lines().

i saw a post that said something like this may be possible "in the next release" but i didn't see what release that was. i'm using 0.9.1. i also saw a reference to coord_munch and it looked like it may almost do the needful but that's about as far as i got.

thanks,
keith

winston - thanks for the followup, much appreciated!

allan - the original data doesn't go below zero but the smoothed data does.  i figured out how to demonstrate the problem more clearly than my original attempts:

> library(ggplot2)
> y<-rep(0:1,each=20,times=5)+runif(10,0,0.05)
> x<-seq(1:length(y))
> ggplot()+geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_smooth(aes(x=x,y=y),method='loess',span=0.20,se=F)

the bottom of the smoothed data dips below y=0 even though the sampled data does not. i wanted to cap the smoothed line to stay above y=0.
keith

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: setting only a single limit on ggplot() coordinates
parts:
On 2012-Jul-11, at 22:31 , keith p. kolley wrote:
>
> allan - the original data doesn't go below zero but the smoothed data does. i figured out how to demonstrate the problem more clearly than my original attempts:
>
>> library(ggplot2)
>> y<-rep(0:1,each=20,times=5)+runif(10,0,0.05)
>> x<-seq(1:length(y))
>> ggplot()+geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_smooth(aes(x=x,y=y),method='loess',span=0.20,se=F)
>
> the bottom of the smoothed data dips below y=0 even though the sampled data does not. i wanted to cap the smoothed line to stay above y=0.
You can discard the points (even smoothed ones) below 0 with scale_y_continuous() or just zoom in to not see them with coord_cartesian()

ggplot()+geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_smooth(aes(x=x,y=y),method='loess',span=0.20,se=F) + scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 1.2))
ggplot()+geom_line(aes(x=x,y=y))+geom_smooth(aes(x=x,y=y),method='loess',span=0.20,se=F) + coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 1.2))

Previously, one was able to supply NA or Inf to one of the limits (instead of 1.2 here) and it ggplot would then use the default computed. This does not seem possible anymore so you have to hard-code a value here, which is not always desirable.

If you want to line to actually become flat at zero, then you need to compute your loess smoother before ggplot and then use geom_path

Jean-Olivier Irisson
